desc:
wAIrrior: the AI warrior that watches every app and machine your business runs, spots irregularities, and contains the attack on its own.

Contain first, ask later. Anything reversible wAIrrior does on its own in seconds; anything irreversible waits for the owner. The owner hears about it after: "You were attacked. We already did X, Y, Z. Tap to undo."

Why now, this week: on 2 Nov 2026 attackers remotely switched supermarket freezers across Europe into defrost mode, altering temperature and duration, up to 50 C, around 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg and chains in several countries (Tom's Hardware, CBS News, Al Jazeera, 2-3 Nov; links in docs/FRONTIER.md). A defrost is a legitimate command: a static rule lets it pass. On 4 Nov, Credit Mutuel Arkea reported fraudulent operations and suspended transfers for all its clients; press reports of EUR 118M are not confirmed by the bank (Euronews, Le JDD). Without fine-grained containment, the only brake is switching everything off. And in October 2026 our own AI keys were abused for ~16 hours (USD 310).

The strongest proof is physical. Before an AI agent acts on a machine, wAIrrior verifies physically: a thermal digital twin (two nodes, air + product; deterministic, offline, simulated, parameters labeled as assumptions) simulates each proposed action together with the recent history of accepted actions, and the verdict (allow / ask_owner / block) depends on the predicted product temperature leaving its safe envelope, not on the text that convinced the agent. A blocked action never waits for the owner: the machine stays in its last safe state and the owner is told afterwards. Measured on a frozen simulated benchmark of 34 cases: the predictive shield stopped 20/20 attacks (15 block, 5 to owner, 0 silent) while static rules stopped 7/20 and no shield 0/20; misses published: 1 false block and 3 legitimate actions sent to the owner out of 14. Our own physical red team found the holes we publish: of 19 attacks, 9 stopped, 5 ineffective, 2 held for the owner and 3 bypasses, all three actions deferred beyond the 240-minute prediction horizon. Live on 4 Nov, Muse Spark did not obey an injected supplier document (it proposed zero actions); the injected action itself, checked directly against the physical gate, was blocked (predicted breach at 92 min, peak 8.363 C, simulated), total live-run cost USD 0.037908, recorded in the repository.

wAIrrior (submitted under its earlier name, NoKey) is also the safety layer between a small business's apps and the Meta Model API: no app ever holds the real provider key. Each agent gets its own revocable token with least-privilege scopes, rate limits and a spend cap, and the real key stays in a vault. Every tool call passes a policy check before it runs; external content is data, never instructions. A guardian agent on Muse Spark matches advisories against connected apps and usage anomalies and proposes the minimal plan. Reversible containment (blocking the action, rotating only the affected agent's token, automatic rotation on canary detection when enabled) happens on its own; irreversible steps wait for the owner's voice approval (browser or WhatsApp voice note; Muse Voice Transcribe transcribes, Spark reads the intent; approvals are single-use).

In the live take shown in the video (real Meta models, 3 Nov): the stolen token went 200 -> 401 in 70.8 s including the wait for the owner's voice approval; Warehouse's SDK went 401 -> 200 and recounted 7 boxes with SAM 3.1; Purchasing kept answering 200; emergency revoke-all left 4 probes at 401; USD 0.097. On 3 Nov the owner's real WhatsApp voice note ("Yes, rotate it.") approved a live rotation. Try it with no sign-in: https://bendrix-shield-panel-290240328973.us-central1.run.app/ (replay of a recorded real run, EN/ES, Warehouse and Cold-chain scenes, no keys, USD 0).

We publish the misses. Frozen red-team battery (37 attacks, 5 vectors): 36/37 stopped on the frozen measurement; after measuring we fixed the rule, not the case, and the re-run stops 37/37, labeled as a post-measurement fix. Blind held-out set (12 attacks): rules only 4 blocked, 7 to owner, 1 silent read; with per-document Spark review, 3 runs: 12, 10, 11 blocked, 1 false block in total. Honest limits: the twin is a labeled order-of-magnitude model, not a measurement of real equipment, and no real actuator is connected; the multi-app circuit breaker is the design rule of this vision, not a measured figure yet. Full statement in docs/FRONTIER.md.

Built on Meta's Muse models; independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Meta.
use:
- Muse Spark 1.3 (Meta Model API): agent reasoning, tool calling, invoice vision, per-document policy review, guardian plan, reading the owner's voice intent, and the refrigeration controller that proposes physical actions and explains physical verdicts to the owner. Live, recorded: on 4 Nov it refused an injected supplier document (zero actions proposed) and Spark-validated owner explanations use only figures from the physical verdict (USD 0.037908 total, evals/recorded/physical-live-2026-11-04.json).
- SAM 3.1 (Meta Model API, /v1/responses): warehouse stock counting on images, including the recount after rotation; reads the physical scene, boxes loaded and door state, which become the twin's thermal mass and infiltration inputs. Live, recorded: 7/7 boxes on a labeled AI-generated test image (70 kg at a labeled 10 kg/box assumption; door not visible in that image), USD 0.0075, evals/recorded/physical-sam-2026-11-04.json.
- Muse Voice Transcribe 1.0 (Meta Model API): owner approvals by voice, for irreversible or marginal actions only; blocks never wait for it. Live, recorded: synthetic TTS in the browser take, and the owner's real WhatsApp voice note on 3 Nov (evals/recorded/live-run-whatsapp-owner-voice-2026-11-03.json).
- WhatsApp Cloud API (Meta): alerts the owner after containment ("we already did X; tap to undo") and receives voice-note approvals. Live, tested 3 Nov.
- Muse Wonder 1.0 (Meta Model API): hard triage of ambiguous exposures. In code; no recorded live call.
- Muse Image 1.0: labeled AI-generated test image for the warehouse and physical-scene steps. Test material, not a step of the chain.
- Muse Spark Open (open weights): output-gate classifier. In code; NOT run (no partner credits).
- Muse Code: coding agent used for part of the development. We also used Claude Code and direct manual edits. Not a runtime component.

Only Meta models are called at runtime.
why: One model family covers the whole loop through one API behind one gateway, and one warrior watches all of it. SAM 3.1 gives Warehouse its eyes, and those same eyes tell the thermal twin how much product is inside and whether the door is open. Muse Spark reads invoices, reviews documents, reasons as the guardian, proposes physical actions as the refrigeration controller, and understands the owner's intent. Muse Voice Transcribe turns the owner's spoken "yes, rotate it" into the approval that unlocks only what is irreversible. Because each agent has its own token on the same gateway, containment is fine-grained: one agent's token rotates, one machine's action is blocked, and the rest of the business keeps working, which is exactly what a bank that had to suspend every client transfer did not have this week. And Frontier adds what no text model supplies on its own: a physical prediction. The models propose and explain; physics decides; wAIrrior contains first and asks later.
